content.title: ARG-1: The Quran's Own Argument (Quran 52:35)
content.body_md:
**In simple words**

Look at yourself. You did not make yourself. And nothing makes itself out of nothing. So Someone made you. That Someone is Allah.

**The steps**

- P1: We exist.
- P2: There are only three options: we came from nothing, OR we made ourselves, OR a Maker made us.
- P3: "From nothing" is impossible (nothing has no power to do anything).
- P4: "Made ourselves" is impossible (a thing must exist before it can act, so it can't create itself).
- C: Therefore a Maker (Allah) made us.

**From the Quran and Sunnah**

Quran 52:35–36 — "Were they created by nothing, or were they the creators [of themselves]? Or did they create the heavens and the earth?"

**Scholars**

Ibn Kathir (tafsir of 52:35), Ibn Uthaymin (explained in islamqa 26745).

**Strongest atheist objection**

This is a false trilemma. Modern physics says the universe may not need a cause in the normal sense; quantum events can look uncaused.

**Best Islamic reply**

The verse is about US and created things, which clearly begin. Even if the physics of the very beginning is debated, the deep point stands: dependent things cannot explain themselves. See ARG-2 and ARG-3.

content.title: ARG-2: Kalam Cosmological Argument (al-Ghazali)
content.body_md:
**In simple words**

Everything that has a starting point was started by something. The universe had a starting point. So something started the universe.

**The steps**

- P1: Whatever begins to exist has a cause.
- P2: The universe began to exist.
- C: The universe has a cause. (That cause is beginningless, immaterial, powerful — this points to God.)

**Scholars**

Abu Hamid al-Ghazali, *Tahafut al-Falasifa (The Incoherence of the Philosophers)* — al-Ghazali argued the universe must have a beginning and thus a cause. Earlier: al-Kindi.

**Strongest atheist objection**

P1 is from everyday experience INSIDE the universe; we can't apply it to the universe as a whole. Also some models have an eternal or quantum-origin universe (Graham Oppy pushes this).

**Best Islamic reply**

"Begins to exist → has a cause" is a very well-supported principle; the alternative (things pop into being from nothing) is worse. Eternal-universe models face the impossibility of a completed infinite past. Mark honestly: the science of t=0 is not fully settled, so lean on the philosophical point, do not overclaim.

**Weak version to AVOID**

Saying "science has PROVEN God with the Big Bang." Too strong. Say it is "consistent with" a beginning.

content.title: ARG-3: Contingency Argument (Ibn Sina / Avicenna)
content.body_md:
**In simple words**

Some things could have not existed (you, trees, stars). They only exist because something else holds them up. This can't go on forever with no foundation. There must be One who exists by Himself and needs nothing. That is Allah — the Necessary Existent (al-Wajib al-Wujud).

**The steps**

- P1: Contingent things exist (things that could have not existed).
- P2: A contingent thing needs something else to explain why it exists.
- P3: The whole collection of contingent things is still contingent, so it too needs an explanation.
- P4: That explanation cannot itself be contingent (or the problem repeats).
- C: There must be a Necessary Being that exists by itself. That is God.

**Scholars**

Ibn Sina (Avicenna), *Burhan al-Siddiqin (Proof of the Truthful)*, in al-Najat and al-Isharat.

**Strongest atheist objection**

This may commit the fallacy of composition — parts being contingent doesn't prove the whole is. Maybe the universe itself is the necessary, brute thing (Russell: 'the universe is just there').

**Best Islamic reply**

The universe is made of changing, dependent parts, so it looks contingent, not necessary. Calling it a "brute fact" just stops asking the question; the contingency argument keeps asking until it reaches a Being that truly needs nothing.

content.title: ARG-4: The Fitrah Argument (Quran 30:30)
content.body_md:
**In simple words**

Deep inside, people naturally feel there is a God, especially in hard moments. Islam says we are born with this feeling (fitrah).

**From the Quran and Sunnah**

30:30 — "So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people."
"No child is born except upon the fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian." — Sahih al-Bukhari 1358 (Book of Funerals; also appears at 1385 and in Tafsir at 4775) and Sahih Muslim 2658 (Book of Destiny). Grade: agreed upon (muttafaqun 'alayhi). Verified on sunnah.com.

**Scholars**

Ibn Taymiyyah wrote a lot on fitrah (Dar' Ta'arud al-'Aql wa'l-Naql).

**Strongest atheist objection**

Feeling something does not make it true. Evolution could give us a 'God instinct' for survival, with no real God behind it (a debunking argument).

**Best Islamic reply**

Fitrah is not the WHOLE proof — it is one sign among many. The intellectual arguments (ARG-1,2,3) plus the fitrah together are strong. And "evolution gave us the feeling" does not prove the feeling is false; it just gives a story of how we got it.

content.title: ARG-5: The Moral Argument
content.body_md:
**In simple words**

We all feel some things are REALLY wrong (torturing a child for fun) — not just "wrong for me." But if there is no God, where do these real, for-everyone rules come from? Islam says they come from God.

**The steps**

- P1: If God does not exist, objective moral values do not exist.
- P2: Objective moral values DO exist.
- C: Therefore God exists.

**Strongest atheist objection**

We can ground morals in human wellbeing, empathy, and society (Sam Harris). No God needed. Also Euthyphro: are things good because God says so (then it's arbitrary), or does God say so because they're good (then good is above God)?

**Best Islamic reply**

Wellbeing-based ethics still can't jump from "is" to "ought" (the is/ought problem). For Euthyphro, see OBJ-4: God's commands flow from His perfectly good NATURE — not arbitrary, and not a standard above Him.

content.title: ARG-6: Consciousness (The Hard Problem)
content.body_md:
**In simple words**

Science can explain how the brain processes signals. But it cannot explain WHY there is a "what it feels like" inside you (the taste of mango, the feeling of red). This inner experience is a mystery for pure matter-only views.

**Strongest atheist objection**

God of the gaps — you point to a thing science hasn't explained YET and say 'God did it.' Science may solve consciousness later.

**Best Islamic reply**

This is not just an unsolved gap; many philosophers argue it is a gap of the WRONG KIND — you cannot get first-person experience out of third-person physical description in principle. Still, present it humbly as a strong pointer, not a knockout "proof."

**Weak version to AVOID**

"Science will NEVER explain anything about the brain." Too strong; only the felt, first-person part is the hard problem.

content.title: ARG-7: Fine-Tuning / Design
content.body_md:
**In simple words**

The numbers of the universe (like the force of gravity) are set in a super-narrow range that allows life. Change them a tiny bit and no life, no stars. This looks designed.

**The steps**

- P1: The constants are fine-tuned for life.
- P2: This is either chance, necessity, or design.
- P3: Chance is wildly unlikely; necessity is unproven.
- C: Design (God) is the best explanation.

**Strongest atheist objection**

The MULTIVERSE: if there are countless universes with random settings, at least one will be life-friendly by chance — and of course we live in that one.

**Best Islamic reply**

The multiverse is not observed; it's an extra, unproven assumption to avoid a Designer. Even if a multiverse exists, a "universe-generator" itself would need setup. Present fine-tuning as a strong probability point, not a certainty.

content.title: OBJ-1: Problem of Evil — Logical Form
content.body_md:
**The objection, said fairly (steelman)**

A God who is all-good, all-powerful, and all-knowing would stop all evil. Evil exists. So such a God does not exist. (Mackie, "Evil and Omnipotence," 1955.)

**Islamic response**

- The logical version is now widely seen as failing, even by many philosophers, because it assumes God can have NO good reason to allow any evil — which is not proven. (Alvin Plantinga's free-will defense broke this.)
- Islam: life is a TEST (Quran 67:2 — "[He] who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed"). A test needs the possibility of hardship and wrong choices.
- Free will: real choice needs the option to do wrong.
- Limited human wisdom: we see a small piece; Allah sees all (see Yaqeen problem-of-evil paper).
- See all of Allah's names TOGETHER: Merciful, Wise, Just — plus perfect justice in the hereafter.

**Likely comeback**

Free will explains human evil, but not disease, earthquakes, or child cancer.

**Notes on strong vs weak answers**

The free-will defense is STRONG for man-made evil. For natural suffering, move to OBJ-3 and the "test + hereafter + limited wisdom" answers.

content.title: OBJ-2: Problem of Evil — Evidential Form
content.body_md:
**The objection, said fairly (steelman)**

Maybe God COULD have reasons for some evil. But the huge amount of apparently pointless suffering makes God UNLIKELY (not impossible). Rowe's example: a fawn burning to death in a forest fire, unseen, helping no one. Draper: the pattern of pain and pleasure fits a "no-God" world better than a God world.

**Islamic response**

- "Appears pointless to us" is not "is pointless." This is the key move (skeptical theism): our knowledge is tiny. Rowe's step from "we see no reason" to "there is no reason" is weak.
- Islam adds a positive story: suffering can raise ranks, erase sins, wake people up, and be perfectly compensated in the hereafter.
- Ibn al-Qayyim: Allah's allowing of evil serves greater goods and wisdoms (see Zeni's Yaqeen paper).

**Likely comeback**

That's an unfalsifiable escape — you just say 'hidden reasons' for anything.

**Notes on strong vs weak answers**

STRONG answer = skeptical theism + hereafter. WEAK answer = pretending we know the exact reason for each tragedy. Don't do that.

content.title: OBJ-3: Animal and Infant Suffering (Hardest Case)
content.body_md:
**The objection, said fairly (steelman)**

Animals and babies have no free will and no sin, yet they suffer terribly. Free-will and test answers seem not to apply.

**Islamic response**

- Human free will still explains much (pollution, neglect, war harming children).
- Islam teaches justice for animals too; there are reports of settling of accounts among creatures on the Day of Judgment.
- A baby who dies is not "punished"; Islam has hope-filled positions about children.
- Limited wisdom + perfect afterlife compensation remain the backbone.

**Notes on strong vs weak answers**

Be gentle and honest. Say clearly: "This is one of the hardest questions; here is how Islam approaches it," not "this is easy."

content.title: OBJ-4: Euthyphro Dilemma
content.body_md:
**The objection, said fairly (steelman)**

Is something good because God commands it, or does God command it because it is good? If the first, morality is arbitrary (God could command cruelty). If the second, goodness is above God, so we don't need God for morality.

**Islamic response**

- This is a FALSE dilemma. God's commands flow from His own perfectly good NATURE. Goodness is not a random choice (not arbitrary), and not a standard outside/above God (not independent). It IS God's nature. So God cannot command cruelty for its own sake, because that would contradict who He is.

**Likely comeback**

Then 'good' just means 'God's nature' — that's defining good into existence / circular.

**Notes on strong vs weak answers**

STRONG answer = grounding in God's nature. This is the mainstream response used by Tzortzis and classical theists.

content.title: OBJ-5: Divine Hiddenness
content.body_md:
**The objection, said fairly (steelman)**

If a loving God wanted a relationship with us, He would make His existence obvious to every honest seeker. But there are sincere "non-resistant non-believers" who look and still don't find Him. So a perfectly loving God probably does not exist. (Schellenberg, *Divine Hiddenness and Human Reason*, Cornell University Press, 1993.)

**Islamic response**

- God is NOT fully hidden: there are signs everywhere (fitrah, the universe, the Quran). The "proof" is available; the test is partly whether we humble ourselves to accept it.
- Faith is meant to be a test (Quran 67:2). Total, forced certainty would remove the test.
- Some "non-resistance" is not as pure as claimed — pride, desire, and environment block the heart.
- Guidance is from Allah; He knows who truly seeks (Quran 16:125 ending).

**Notes on strong vs weak answers**

Answer with humility; don't accuse a specific person of secretly resisting. Talk about signs + the wisdom of a test.

content.title: OBJ-6: Who Created God?
content.body_md:
**The objection, said fairly (steelman)**

If everything needs a cause/designer, then God needs one too. If God can be uncaused, why not just say the universe is uncaused and skip God?

**Islamic response**

- The principle is NOT "everything needs a cause." It is "everything that BEGINS to exist needs a cause." God did not begin; He is the Necessary Being. So the question is a category mistake.
- An endless chain of creators (infinite regress) is impossible; the chain must stop at an uncaused First.
- The Prophet ﷺ told us this doubt comes from Shaytan: "Satan comes to one of you and says, 'Who created so-and-so?' till he says, 'Who created your Lord?' When he does that, let him seek refuge with Allah and stop." — Sahih al-Bukhari 3276, Sahih Muslim 134 (agreed upon; verified on sunnah.com). (A separate narration adds saying "Amantu billah" — I believe in Allah.)

**Notes on strong vs weak answers**

STRONG and simple. Just fix the false principle ("begins to exist").

content.title: OBJ-7: I Can Be Good Without God
content.body_md:
**The objection, said fairly (steelman)**

Atheists live moral lives, give to charity, love their families. So we don't need God to be good.

**Islamic response**

- Two different questions: (a) CAN an atheist ACT good? Yes, of course. (b) Can atheism JUSTIFY that some things are REALLY, objectively wrong? That's the hard part.
- Without God, "good" tends to become just opinion, feelings, or what society agrees on — which can change. See ARG-5 and Mackie's admission.

**Notes on strong vs weak answers**

Never say atheists are bad people. That's a strawman and rude. Separate "living good" from "grounding good."

**Islamic response**

- Science explains HOW things work inside nature; it does not answer WHY there is anything at all, or ground morality, meaning, or consciousness (see ARG-6).
- "Only science gives truth" is itself NOT a scientific claim — it's a philosophy claim, so it defeats itself (self-refuting).
- Islam loves science; the Quran invites us to study nature (Quran 3:190–191). No conflict between studying creation and believing in the Creator.

**Notes on strong vs weak answers**

STRONG. WEAK version to avoid: attacking evolution with bad science, or claiming "scientific miracles in the Quran" as knockout proof (over-claiming — many scholars warn against this).

content.title: OBJ-11: Kalam Objections (Quantum / Eternal Universe)

content.title: OBJ-15: Hume on Miracles
content.body_md:
**The objection, said fairly (steelman)**

Hume (*Enquiry*, "Of Miracles"): a miracle breaks the laws of nature, which have the strongest possible evidence. It's always more likely the witness lied or was fooled than that a law broke. So never believe a miracle on testimony.

**Islamic response**

- Hume's rule can be too strong: it would make us reject any truly new event. Probability should follow the quality and quantity of evidence, not rule miracles out in advance.
- The Quran's main "sign" is not a one-off physical trick but a lasting, examinable text (its challenge to produce the like of it).

content.title: What is an argument?
content.body_md:
An argument = reasons (premises) that lead to a point (conclusion). Example:
- P1: All humans die.
- P2: I am a human.
- C: I will die.

content.title: Valid vs Sound (very important)
content.body_md:
- **Valid** = the SHAPE is right. If premises were true, the conclusion would HAVE to be true.
- **Sound** = valid AND the premises are actually TRUE.
- A valid argument can still be wrong if a premise is false. Always check: (a) Is the shape valid? (b) Are the premises true?

content.title: How to Steelman (do this always)
content.body_md:
1. Repeat their argument in your own words.
2. Make it as STRONG and fair as you can.
3. Ask: "Did I get that right?"
4. THEN answer. (This builds trust and is better dawah — Quran 16:125.)

content.title: Socratic Method (asking good questions)
content.body_md:
Instead of lecturing, ask gentle questions so the person thinks:
- "What do you mean exactly by 'proof'?"
- "Would anything ever change your mind? What would?"
- "If there's no objective right and wrong, was any historical atrocity REALLY wrong, or just disliked?"
- "Where do you think the universe came from?"
Good questions open hearts better than winning points.

content.title: Burden of Proof
content.body_md: Whoever makes a claim must support it. "There is no God" is also a claim (for a strong atheist). "I'm not convinced" (agnostic) is different. Ask them which one they mean.

content.title: The Golden Verses
content.body_md:
- **16:125** — Invite with (a) wisdom, (b) good preaching, (c) arguing in the BEST way.
- **3:159** — Be gentle; harshness pushes people away.
- **28:56** — You cannot guide anyone; only Allah guides. So relax and be kind; results aren't on you.
- **41:34** — Answer bad with good; an enemy can become a close friend.

content.title: First: Find the ROOT of their doubt
content.body_md:
Ask kindly. Three main roots:
1. **Intellectual doubt** — they want reasons/evidence. → Give arguments + sources (files 01–03).
2. **Bad experience / pain** — hurt by family, community, trauma. → Listen first. Don't debate a wound.
3. **No exposure** — they just never learned real Islam. → Share clearly and simply.
Matching the answer to the root is the whole game.

content.title: Common mistakes of young du'at (avoid!)
content.body_md:
- Arrogance / wanting to "win" instead of guide.
- Mocking atheists or their heroes (breaks 16:125).
- Over-claiming ("science PROVES the Quran," "this is 100% certain").
- Debating to show off in public.
- Talking about very deep philosophy before you're ready (can shake your own faith).
- Forgetting dua — guidance is from Allah (28:56).

content.title: Protecting YOUR OWN faith
content.body_md:
- **Waswas (whispers):** intrusive doubts about God. The Prophet ﷺ said to seek refuge in Allah and STOP engaging (Bukhari 3276, Muslim 134). A separate narration: say "Amantu billah" (I believe in Allah). Then change what you're doing (stand up, make wudu, pray).
- **Don't argue with waswas in your head** — that feeds it.
- **Separate waswas from real questions:** waswas = repeating, shameful, no real trigger → seek refuge. Real question = wants evidence → study + ask scholars.
- **Cautions on deep philosophy (scholars):** al-Ghazali (in islamqa 88184) split philosophy into parts — logic/math are useful; some metaphysics can harm the weak. islamqa 99983: only those grounded in Quran and Sunnah should dive deep, so they can tell truth from error. So: build your basics FIRST, keep good company, keep worship strong, and take doubts to real scholars (islamqa.org 169537).
- **Keep a "faith routine":** daily Quran, dhikr, salah, good friends (a person follows the way of their close friend).

content.title: A simple dawah flow
content.body_md:
1. Greet warmly, build rapport.
2. Ask questions; find the root.
3. Steelman their view.
4. Give ONE clear point with a source.
5. Ask a gentle Socratic question.
6. Make dua for them. Leave the door open. Guidance is Allah's job.
**52:35–36** — "Were they created by nothing, or were they the creators?" → We must have a Maker. (Main Quranic argument.)
**30:30** — "…the fitrah of Allah upon which He created people…" → We're born knowing God.
**67:2** — "[He] who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed." → Life is a test. (Verified: Surah Al-Mulk, verse 2.)
**51:56** — "I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me." → Our purpose.
**16:125** — "Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue in the best way." → How to do dawah.
**3:159** — "By the mercy of Allah you were gentle with them…" → Be gentle.
**28:56** — "You do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills." → Guidance is from Allah, not us.
**41:34** — "Repel [evil] by that which is better…" → Answer harshness with kindness.
**3:190–191** — Signs in the heavens and earth for people who think. → Islam invites reflection on nature.
**41:53** — "We will show them Our signs… until it becomes clear that it is the truth." → Signs point to God.
**4:82** — "Do they not reflect upon the Quran?" → Reflection is invited.

content.title: How debates are scored (0–5 each, total /30)
content.body_md:
Judge the USER's answer on:
1. **Logic** — valid/sound? avoided fallacies?
2. **Accuracy of Islamic sources** — correct verses/hadith/fatwas? (No invented ones!)
3. **Understanding the opponent** — did they steelman and address the REAL point?
4. **Clarity** — simple, clear, well-organized?
5. **Adab / kindness** — gentle, respectful, no mocking (16:125, 3:159)?
6. **Avoiding overclaim** — didn't exaggerate ("proven!", "scientific miracle")?

**Bands:** 26–30 Excellent; 20–25 Strong; 14–19 Okay; 8–13 Weak; 0–7 Needs work.

### Example feedback format
- **Score:** 22/30 (Strong)
- **What was strong:** "You steelmanned the problem of evil and used Quran 67:2 correctly."
- **What was weak:** "You said science 'proves' God — that's an overclaim. Also you didn't answer the fawn example."
- **Better sample answer:** "[model answer]"
- **Sources to review:** OBJ-2, ARG-2.
- **Adab note:** "Great tone — kind and calm."

flashcards.back: Yes: things that begin need a cause; the universe began; you didn't make yourself (Quran 52:35).

flashcards.back: It's made of changing, dependent parts, so it looks contingent, not necessary.
The inborn feeling that God is real (Quran 30:30; Bukhari 1358).

flashcards.front: Isn't "God did it" just a gap-filler?
flashcards.back: Only weak if it's a temporary gap; consciousness may be a deeper, in-principle gap.

flashcards.back: The universe began, so it has a cause.

flashcards.front: Doesn't quantum physics show things come from nothing?
flashcards.back: No — a quantum vacuum is not "nothing"; it has fields and laws.

flashcards.back: It fits a beginning, but don't over-claim "proof"; lean on the logic.

flashcards.back: Because a Necessary Being exists and gives being to all else.

flashcards.front: If God is good, why is there evil?
flashcards.back: Life is a test (67:2); free will; limited human wisdom; justice in the afterlife.

flashcards.front: Why do babies and animals suffer?
flashcards.back: Hardest case; Islam affirms justice for all and hope for children; limited wisdom + afterlife.
No — it's honest humility about our tiny knowledge, plus a positive afterlife story.
No; at most it raises a hard question, fully answered by test + wisdom + hereafter.
Yes, they can ACT good; the question is whether atheism can GROUND real right and wrong.

flashcards.front: Why do we need God for morality?
flashcards.back: Without God, "good" tends to become opinion or feeling, not objective.
That objective values would make God more probable (so he denied objective values).

flashcards.front: Euthyphro: is good good because God says so?
flashcards.back: False dilemma; good flows from God's perfectly good NATURE.
No more than any bedrock explanation; it stops the regress at the best place.

flashcards.front: Can't science tell us right from wrong?
flashcards.back: No — you can't get "ought" from "is" (is/ought problem).
It explains HOW nature works, not WHY anything exists, or meaning, or consciousness.
Why we have inner felt experience at all (Chalmers, 1995).
No; the Quran invites study of nature (3:190–191).

flashcards.front: Are there scientific miracles in the Quran?
flashcards.back: Be careful; many scholars say don't lean on these as proofs.

flashcards.front: If Allah decreed everything, am I free?
flashcards.back: Yes; Allah's knowledge doesn't force you; you truly choose.

flashcards.front: Is it fair to be judged for a decreed life?
flashcards.back: We don't know our decree and we feel/use real choice daily.
Judgment matches the person's true state and rejection; mercy is vast.

flashcards.front: Why Islam and not another religion?
flashcards.back: Move to Quran + Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ evidence + pure tawhid.

flashcards.front: You only believe because you were born Muslim?
flashcards.back: Origin doesn't decide truth (genetic fallacy); same applies to atheists.
Follow the evidence's quality; the Quran is a lasting, testable sign.

flashcards.front: Life has no meaning without God?
flashcards.back: Islam gives real, given purpose (51:56); invented meaning is fragile.
He's not fully hidden — signs everywhere; and faith is a test.

flashcards.front: Is it wrong to have doubts?
flashcards.back: No; doubts are normal. Seek knowledge and ask scholars (islamqa.org 169537).
Seek refuge in Allah, say "Amantu billah," stop arguing with it, change activity.

flashcards.front: How should I start a dawah talk?
flashcards.back: Be warm, ask questions, find the root of their doubt.

flashcards.front: What if I don't know the answer?
flashcards.back: Say so honestly and offer to find it.
No; aim to guide gently; guidance is from Allah (28:56).

flashcards.front: Is the contingency argument a composition fallacy?
flashcards.back: No — the universe's parts are all dependent, so the whole is too.

flashcards.front: Does divine command theory make morality arbitrary?
flashcards.back: No — commands flow from God's necessary good nature.

flashcards.front: How is the Quran's "miracle" different from Hume's target?

The view that we can't expect to see all of God's reasons.

flashcards.front: What's the best SINGLE opener argument?

flashcards.front: How to talk to someone grieving?

flashcards.back: When it's mockery/bad-faith; protect your peace and faith.

quizzes.question: The kalam argument says the universe has a cause because:

choices.text: Whatever BEGINS to exist has a cause, and the universe began

quizzes.explanation: A is too strong (God didn't begin); the correct principle is about things that BEGIN.

quizzes.question: The best answer to Euthyphro is:

choices.text: Good is whatever God randomly commands
Good flows from God's perfectly good nature

quizzes.explanation: C escapes both horns of the false dilemma.

quizzes.question: When someone is grieving and angry at God, you should FIRST:

choices.text: Tell them it's just a test and move on

quizzes.explanation: Match the answer to the ROOT (pain, not intellect).

quizzes.question: "You only believe because you were born Muslim" is which fallacy?
quizzes.explanation: It judges a belief by its ORIGIN, not its truth.

quizzes.question: Which is an OVERCLAIM to avoid?
An argument is VALID when:

choices.text: All of its premises are true
If the premises were true, the conclusion would have to be true

quizzes.explanation: Valid is about the SHAPE. Sound is stronger: valid AND the premises are really true.

quizzes.question: What is a "contingent" thing?

choices.text: Something that must exist and cannot not exist
Something that could have not existed, and depends on something else

quizzes.explanation: You, a tree and a star are contingent. A necessary being is the opposite: it must exist and depends on nothing.

quizzes.question: What does "steelman" mean?

choices.text: Twisting the other side into a weak version
Saying the other side’s view in its strongest, fairest form first
Refusing to listen to the other side

quizzes.explanation: The opposite is a strawman, which is a fallacy. Steelmanning builds trust and is better dawah (16:125).

quizzes.question: Quran 52:35–36 gives three options. Which one does the verse leave standing?
quizzes.explanation: "From nothing" is impossible because nothing has no power. "Made ourselves" is impossible because a thing must exist before it can act.

quizzes.question: What is the best answer to "Who created God?"

choices.text: Nobody knows, it is a mystery
The principle is not "everything needs a cause" but "everything that BEGINS to exist needs a cause" — and God never began
Science will answer this one day

quizzes.explanation: The question mixes up the principle. Fixing the principle answers it. The Prophet ﺳ also told us to seek refuge in Allah when this whisper comes (Bukhari 3276, Muslim 134).

quizzes.question: An endless backwards chain of causes (infinite regress) is a problem because:

choices.text: It is too hard to imagine
Many scholars argue a real, completed endless past chain is impossible, so the chain must stop at an uncaused First
Science has measured the exact start
The Quran forbids thinking about it

quizzes.explanation: This is the philosophical point behind both ARG-2 and OBJ-6. Do not claim science has settled the first instant.

quizzes.question: What should you do FIRST in a dawah conversation?

choices.text: Give your strongest argument straight away
Find the ROOT of their doubt by asking kindly
Quote as many hadith as you can

quizzes.explanation: The three roots are: intellectual doubt, pain or bad experience, and no exposure. Matching the answer to the root is the whole game.

quizzes.question: Quran 16:125 tells us to invite with:

choices.text: Wisdom, good preaching, and arguing in the best way

quizzes.explanation: 3:159 adds that harshness pushes people away, and 28:56 reminds us that only Allah guides.

quizzes.question: What should you say when you do NOT know an answer?

choices.text: Make a good guess so you do not look weak
Say honestly that you do not know, and offer to find out or point to a scholar
Say the question is not allowed

quizzes.explanation: This is honest and strong. Guessing or making up a hadith is a sin and destroys trust.

quizzes.question: How should you present the Big Bang when giving the kalam argument?

choices.text: Science has PROVEN God with the Big Bang
The evidence is consistent with a beginning, and the main weight is on the philosophical point
Physics has nothing to say about it

quizzes.explanation: File 01 marks "science has PROVEN God" as a weak version to AVOID. The science of the first instant is debated, so lean on the philosophy.

quizzes.question: An atheist says quantum particles appear without a cause. The best reply is:

choices.text: A quantum vacuum is not "nothing" — it has fields and laws, so this is not something from nothing

quizzes.explanation: Be honest that the physics is debated. Answer the real point instead of attacking science.

quizzes.question: Which atheist philosopher admitted objective values would make God more probable?
quizzes.explanation: Mackie wrote this in The Miracle of Theism (1982), then escaped the conclusion by denying that objective values exist (his "error theory").

quizzes.question: "I can be good without God" is best answered by:

choices.text: Separating two questions: CAN an atheist act good (yes), and can atheism GROUND real right and wrong (the hard part)

quizzes.explanation: Never say atheists are bad people — that is a strawman and rude. Separate "living good" from "grounding good".

quizzes.question: Which fallacy blocks getting morality from science alone?

choices.text: The is/ought fallacy — jumping from facts to values with no bridge

quizzes.explanation: Wellbeing-based ethics still cannot cross from "is" to "ought". This is the key point against science-based morality.

quizzes.question: What is the fitrah?

choices.text: The inborn, natural feeling every human has that God is real
A kind of proof from science

quizzes.explanation: Quran 30:30 and the hadith "every child is born upon the fitrah" (Bukhari 1358, Muslim 2658, agreed upon).

quizzes.question: An atheist says evolution gave us a "God instinct", so the fitrah proves nothing. Best reply:

choices.text: Explaining HOW we got a belief does not show the belief is FALSE — and fitrah is one sign among many, not the whole proof
The fitrah is the only proof we need

quizzes.explanation: Present fitrah together with the intellectual arguments (ARG-1, 2, 3), not on its own.

quizzes.question: The correct order when you steelman is:

choices.text: Answer first, then repeat their view
Repeat their argument in your own words, make it as strong as you can, ask "did I get that right?", THEN answer
Say their view is silly, then answer
Only ask questions and never answer

quizzes.explanation: This builds trust and is better dawah (Quran 16:125).

quizzes.question: The LOGICAL problem of evil is now widely seen as failing because:

choices.text: It assumes God can have NO good reason to allow any evil, which is not proven

quizzes.explanation: Plantinga’s free-will defence broke the logical version. Islam adds: life is a test (Quran 67:2), free will, and limited human wisdom.

quizzes.question: Rowe’s fawn example (an animal burning unseen in a forest fire) is best answered by:

choices.text: Pointing out that "we see no reason" is not the same as "there is no reason", plus perfect compensation in the hereafter
Saying animals do not feel pain
Giving the exact reason God allowed it

quizzes.explanation: This is skeptical theism. File 02 warns that pretending to know the exact reason for one tragedy is a WEAK answer.

quizzes.question: How should you talk about animal and infant suffering?

choices.text: Say it is an easy question
Say clearly that it is one of the hardest questions, then show how Islam approaches it
Say the person is sinning for asking

quizzes.explanation: Be gentle and honest. Never say "this is easy".

quizzes.question: Schellenberg’s hiddenness argument is best answered by:

choices.text: Saying every non-believer is secretly dishonest
Showing that God is not fully hidden (signs, fitrah, the Quran) and that faith is meant to be a test
Saying God does not want a relationship

quizzes.explanation: Answer with humility. Do not accuse a specific person of secretly resisting.

quizzes.question: On qadr and free will, the mainstream Islamic position is:

choices.text: Humans have no free will at all (Jabarites)
Allah has no control over our acts (Qadarites)
BOTH Allah’s decree AND real human choice — Allah’s knowledge does not force you

quizzes.explanation: Both extremes are rejected. Say honestly that this is subtle, and even great scholars call it hard for the mind to fully grasp.

quizzes.question: When someone says eternal hell is unfair, a careful answer includes:

choices.text: Punishment matches the person’s state and their rejection, Allah’s mercy is vast, and scholars differ on some details
The topic should never be discussed

quizzes.explanation: File 02 says to keep to the mainstream and to flag honestly where scholars differ. Handle this gently, especially with someone in pain.

quizzes.question: An ex-Muslim says "Don’t lecture me." What is the first thing to do?

choices.text: Find the real root — intellectual doubt, pain, or no exposure — by asking, not lecturing
Tell them they just want to sin

quizzes.explanation: Ex-Muslim doubts are often a MIX of intellect and pain. Never say "you just want to sin". Separate bad Muslims from Islam itself.

quizzes.question: With an emotional doubter you should mostly give:

choices.text: Comfort, presence, dua and patience — fewer arguments

quizzes.explanation: Intellectual doubters need clear logic and honest sources. Many people are BOTH — watch their words and feelings.

quizzes.question: What is the cure for waswas (repeating whispers of doubt)?

choices.text: Argue with the thought until it goes away
Seek refuge in Allah, say "Amantu billah", stop engaging, and change what you are doing
Ignore your faith for a while

quizzes.explanation: Arguing with waswas feeds it (Bukhari 3276, Muslim 134). Note: the "Amantu billah" wording is a SEPARATE narration, not part of Bukhari 3276.

quizzes.question: Who named the "hard problem of consciousness"?
quizzes.explanation: Chalmers, "Facing Up to the Problem of Consciousness", Journal of Consciousness Studies 2(3):200–219 (1995).

quizzes.question: Why is the hard problem argued to be MORE than a normal "gap"?

choices.text: Because many philosophers argue you cannot get first-person felt experience from third-person physical description even in principle

quizzes.explanation: Still present it humbly as a strong pointer, not a knockout proof. Do not say science will never explain anything about the brain.

quizzes.question: The best reply to the multiverse answer to fine-tuning is:

choices.text: It is unobserved, adds huge unproven machinery, and a universe-generator would itself need setup

quizzes.explanation: Present fine-tuning as a strong probability point, not a certainty.

quizzes.question: Why is "only what science can test is real" self-refuting?

choices.text: Because that statement itself cannot be tested by science — it is a philosophy claim

quizzes.explanation: Islam loves science: the Quran invites us to study nature (3:190–191). Avoid attacking evolution with bad science.

quizzes.question: Hume’s argument against miracles is best answered by:

choices.text: Saying laws of nature do not exist
Showing his rule is too strong — it would reject any truly new event — and that the Quran’s main sign is a lasting, examinable text

quizzes.question: The contingency argument concludes that there must be:

choices.text: A Necessary Being that exists by itself and needs nothing

quizzes.explanation: Ibn Sina called this the Necessary Existent (al-Wajib al-Wujud), in his Burhan al-Siddiqin.

quizzes.question: Is the contingency argument a composition fallacy?

choices.text: No — the universe is made of changing, dependent parts, so it looks contingent rather than necessary

quizzes.explanation: Calling the universe a "brute fact" just stops asking the question. The contingency argument keeps asking until it reaches something that truly needs nothing.
